access_links.label: Improving Communication of Flood Forecasts on the U.S. Climate Resilience Toolkit

description: Improving Communication of Flood Forecasts is a case study listed in U.S. Climate Resilience Toolkit, a national climate-adaptation toolkit, published or maintained by NOAA National Weather Service | North Central River Forecast Center; International Water Institute; Houston Engineering Inc.. When a flood is forecast for the Red River of the North, community leaders, emergency responders, and residents around Fargo, North Dakota, and Moorhead, Minnesota, can gauge their need for preparation. They use tools to produce visualizations showing the extent, depth, and timing of expected flooding. Coverage: Minnesota (2015). The toolkit gives Minnesota as the location, 2015 as the year. The listed link gives the documented application. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is not stated on the toolkit page (no licence or terms statement seen). Caveats: this record was written from the toolkit page, which was read; the cited source documents and the outcomes reported were not checked, and no model or dataset used was verified. It can support comparison with similar adaptation projects and planning precedents. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-us-climate-resilience-toolkit-catalogue.
